items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: That went to Fort Worth. Paul Barnes, saxophone.

ctx.x: That went to Fort Worth. Paul Barnes, saxophone. Chinese, drummer. John Marrero, banjo. Simon Marrero, bass. Celestine, cornet. William Ridgely, trombone. Emma Barrett, saxophone. Piano.

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: So when I got in the band, around the last part of the Tuxedo band, and they came up with a little confusion between Ridgely, the manager of the band, and Papa Celestad.

ctx.x: That was Celestad. Celestad and Pierron and they were big society bands, you see. And they'd make more money. So I joined Celestad's band, Tuxedo band. They'd heard Rene very much because he liked it so much. He hated it. But there was nothing you could do but I was making more money and everything else. So I worked with the Tuxedo band. And the Tuxedo band, that's what, that's called an original Tuxedo band. And that was long before my time, payback time, and Johnny Sincere, Kirok, we went out with nothing but a…
Oh I see, they had fallen out. I want to ask you, Paul, why did Ridgely and Celestad fall out? They just didn't agree about running the band?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: He tried to come back and get me to set up a bunch of guards, but I didn't want to do it the same time.

ctx.x: That banjo player? No, right there. Trumpet player? That's Kid Thomas from across the river. Oh, I see. Paul Barnes. He never did come back. He didn't make it so good.

He never did come back. He didn't make it so good. Bonds is back here. I knew he did. Yeah, but he seems to have trouble with his clarinet playing. He can't play it like he… I know he's not doing what he thinks he can do. Yeah. He got himself rated a little above. He tried to come back and get me to set up a bunch of guards, but I didn't want to do it the same time.
No. I want to play a tape for you here, if I can find it.
